tools.name: get_my_applications
tools.description: Get the user's vacancy application records with filtering and search. Returns applications the user has created (saved, applied, rejected, etc.) along with vacancy summary for each: id, status, notes, vacancyId, timestamps, and a vacancy summary (title, companyName, link, expiresAt, salary, source). The vacancy's `link` is its page on onetap.work and the only URL to give the user. Offset pagination (page/limit); the response carries `total`.

tools.name: get_vacancy
tools.description: Get full details of a specific vacancy by ID or onetap.work URL. Returns: id, title, companyName, link, descriptionText, salary ({ min, max, currency, period } or null), cities, workplaceType[], experienceLevels[], employmentTypes[], publishedAt, expiresAt, source info, and the user's application status. `link` is the only URL to give the user.

tools.name: get_apply_target
tools.description: Get the external address where an application for this vacancy is actually submitted. Returns { vacancyId, title, companyName, url, kind, pageUrl }: kind='direct' means url is the employer's application form; kind='source' means url is the original job-board posting, where you still have to find the apply control yourself. FOR YOUR NAVIGATION ONLY: never print `url` in your reply, never turn it into a link, never hand it to the user. Everything you show the user points at `pageUrl`.

tools.name: count_applications_by_status
tools.description: Count the user's applications grouped by pipeline status. Every status is a key of the result, zero-filled.

tools.name: update_application_status
tools.description: Create or update the user's application record for ONE vacancy (upsert). Use NOT_INTERESTED to dismiss, ARCHIVED to shelve.

tools.name: bulk_update_applications
tools.description: Move up to 50 vacancies through the application pipeline in one call. Each item carries its own notes.

tools.name: search_vacancies
tools.description: Search for job vacancies with filters. Returns { total, maxExactCount, vacancies[], nextCursor }; every result carries its full descriptionText. Keywords are OR'd full-text terms.
